slides.texte_overlay:
small social dares that quietly
rebuilt my confidence

eating alone in public

i took myself out for dinner alone once a week, no phone on the table. the first time felt awful, by the third time i was enjoying it, and now very little scares me.

the honest opinion

when friends asked where to eat or what to watch, i stopped saying i don't mind and gave a real answer. tiny opinions are practice for the moments when your voice really matters.

asking the question

in every class or meeting, i made myself ask one question out loud, even a simple one. after a month, speaking in front of a group felt normal instead of terrifying.

having something to say

i spent 5 minutes a day learning one fascinating thing: a strange animal, a lost city, a famous painting. walking into a room with something to talk about changed everything.
slides.texte_sophia:
having something to say

i used to dread small talk. now i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app: a strange animal, a lost city. walking in with something to talk about changed everything.

slides.texte_overlay:
wearing the bold thing

i wore the outfit i usually saved for special days on a normal tuesday. people noticed for about ten seconds, and i realised everyone is far too busy to judge me.
